actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species occurs at low and moderate elevations from Jalisco on the Pacific versant, and from northern Taumalipas on the Atlantic versant of Mexico, south and east through Central America, exclusive of the Pacific versant of southern Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and southwestern Panama; it has also introduced and established in southern Florida. Two records exist for Colombia, however these are misidentifications (Gutiérrez-Cárdenas et al. in review); previous references to this species' occurrence in northwestern Colombia are considered to be in error (Savage 2002). In the Yucatan Peninsula, it is pan-peninsular. It occurs at elevations from about sea level up to about 1,500 meters (Koehler 2008).
documentation.population: This is one of the most common reptiles throughout its range.
documentation.habitats: This species can be found in tropical and subtropical wet, moist, and dry forest. It occurs in dense vegetation along the margin of practically any body of water.  It is very tolerant of disturbed habitats. It is an egg-laying species.
documentation.threats: There are no known threats to this species.
documentation.measures: Currently, this species is of relatively low conservation concern and does not require significant additional protection or major management, monitoring, or research action. Its range includes several protected areas.
documentation.use_trade: This species appears in the international pet trade.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern because it is very widespread, common, and very adaptable to habitat alteration, and its population is stable.
